CharacterArchiveContent.14211.2.en:
Cosette has a small fridge in her room.
It's tucked away in the corner, behind the wardrobe, and covered with a small curtain. The door is decorated with various cute magnets and a tiny memo board, with a doodle of flowers that Cosette had drawn.

Each morning, before heading out, Cosette opens the fridge and picks her "reward" for the day from the neatly stacked bottles inside.
Yesterday, she had coconut flavor fruit milk.
Today, a bitter tea to balance things out.
Tomorrow?
By tomorrow, the fridge will be one-third empty—Time to restock!

Where there are "rewards," there are also "punishments."
Once, when she didn't execute her mission perfectly, Cosette reflected on the failure at bedtime and "punished" herself by not having any "reward" drinks for a whole week.
In the following days, the fridge remained untouched.
One week later, she opened the fridge and discovered that last week's fresh milk had turned sour. Cosette took a sip, then added sugar to make it taste just the way she liked it.
That night, Cosette almost vomited her guts out. That's when she learned from the doctor that fridge couldn't keep things fresh indefinitely; when milk turned sour, it didn't magically become yogurt. Cosette watched tearfully as the doctor threw away all the expired drinks that she cherished too much to drink."You can't get those cilantro-flavored yogurt anymore... And that's my last case...""It expired two months ago; it should've been in the waste bin long ago."

The fridge was almost empty, time to replenish her stock.
Cosette picked up a pen and wrote a memo on the board:"Yogurt and milk only last a week, don't buy too much."
CharacterArchiveContent.14211.2.cn:
珂赛特的房间里藏着一个冰箱。
它被放在珂赛特房间里的角落里，藏在衣柜的后面，用一个小帘子挡着，冰箱门被各种形状可爱的冰箱贴装饰着，还挂着一个小小的留言板，上面还留着上次珂赛特随手画上去的小花。

珂赛特会在每天早上出门前打开这个冰箱，从堆码整齐的饮料里，选出今天的“奖励”。
昨天是椰子口味的果奶。
那今天可以是苦味的甘茶。
明天的话……
冰箱已经空出三分之一了，该补货了！

有“奖励”就会有“惩罚”。
任务完成得并不完美。珂赛特在睡前进行自我反省，“惩罚”自己接下来一周都不可以有“奖励”。
于是冰箱一周没有被打开过。
一周之后，上周的鲜奶变成了酸奶，珂赛特尝了一口，又自己加了点糖，变成了她喜欢的酸甜口味。
只可惜当天晚上，当珂赛特上吐下泻的时候，才从医生那得知，冰箱并不是万能的，牛奶变酸是变质不是变成酸奶。最终含泪看着医生把她冰箱里那些舍不得喝却已过期的饮料扔掉。
“香菜口味的酸奶买不到了，那是最后一盒……”
“都过期两个月了，早该扔了。”

冰箱好空，要去补货才行。
珂赛特拿过笔，在冰箱门上的留言板写下提醒自己的留言：
“酸奶和牛奶最多存放一周，别买太多。”

CharacterArchiveContent.14212.2.en:
What kind of place is Nova?

The atmosphere within Nocturn Eterna has been restive lately. Everyone seems on edge. The other girls told Cosette that there was a big plan in the works and it could change the future for all Bayans.
—A chance to bring a better life to everyone.
What would a better life look like? The girls chatter excitedly about their dreams for the future: proper homes, a warm and cozy room with hearty meals in the cold winter. They've heard of something called cake—soft, sweet, and fragrant—and they wonder what it would be like to taste even a single bite...
Cosette trails in the line behind Aeloria, glancing curiously around. She isn't really interested in what the others are talking about. She doesn't feel much sense of belonging to Nocturn Eterna. What she cares about is Aeloria's mission, and whether there's something she can do to help.

To Cosette, the people of Nocturn Eterna aren't much different from those of her old village.
Under the guise of taking in orphans, they brought Cosette and a dozen other children away, promising food, shelter, even education. In reality, they shut the children in a cramped room, giving them just enough to stay alive, with no freedom of movement, let alone "education."
Cosette spent an entire winter in that tiny room. After that, people began to show up, taking away children one by one. In the end, only Cosette remained.
The guards didn't bother to hide their chatter: children deemed useless would be sent back to their villages. Cosette overheard them but thought going back didn't sound so bad. At least there, she could still rummage freely through the trash piles.

And it was on that very day that Aeloria appeared.
She took Cosette in, gave her food and clothing, a place to stay, meals that filled her belly. She even taught her to read and how to use magic.
Thus when Aeloria received a new mission, Cosette looked up at her, full with expectation.
"Is there anything I can do to help? No matter what it is, I'll give it my all!"
Aeloria's expression grew complicated, and in the end she sighed.
"Then come with me to the continent of Nova. As a Sleeper, you'll blend into Novian society and remain hidden until I summon you." 
"But before that, you must learn the magic that conceals your horns."
Cosette's eyes gleamed with confidence.
"I'll succeed for sure, Lady Aeloria!"

The journey from Baya to Nova is a blur in Cosette's memory—perhaps from excitement, perhaps from nervousness. By the time she comes to her senses, her group of Sleepers has already scaled a cliffside waterfall and reached a dense forest.
Standing on this land, Cosette sees green stretching in every direction, all of it brimming with life. The breeze stirs, insects and birds sing together—a sight and sound unknown in Baya.
She turns back to glance at the waterfall behind her, its torrents leaping into the unseen depths below.
So this is what Nova's world is like.
Cosette lingers quietly for a while, then she shoulders her backpack. With a map in hand and her mission ahead, she steps forward into an entirely new adventure.
CharacterArchiveContent.14212.2.cn:
诺瓦的世界，是个什么样的地方？

永夜内部最近似乎有些动荡，所有人都紧绷着，零零碎碎的情报在女孩们之间的低语中传递，听下来似乎是，永夜有个很重要的计划要开始实施，这关系到拜雅人的未来。
如果成功了，大家都会过上好的生活。
好生活是什么样的？女孩们七嘴八舌地畅想未来，想要完整的房子，想要不挨冻的冬天，想要热乎乎的食物，听说有一种叫蛋糕的东西香香软软，如果可以尝一口的话……
珂赛特跟在极光身后的队伍里，好奇地四处张望，对身边人讨论的事情并没有太大的兴趣。她对永夜没有太多归属感，她更好奇极光的任务会是什么，有什么是自己可以帮上忙的。

对珂赛特而言，永夜的人和她原本村子里的人并没有太大区别。
他们以收留孤儿的名义带走了珂赛特和十几个孩子，号称会给孩子们温饱和住宿，甚至教育。但事实上，他们把十几个孩子被关在小小的房间里，提供仅能能维持生命体征的食物，没有活动的自由，更别谈所谓“教育”。
珂赛特在那个小房间里度过了一个寒冬，在那之后，陆陆续续有人出现，挑走了一些孩子，然后带着那些孩子离开，渐渐的，人越来越少，直到最后，剩下珂赛特一个。
看守的侍卫没有避讳地闲聊，没有用的孩子会被送回村子。珂赛特听见了，但珂赛特觉得回去也挺好，起码，在村子里她还能自由地去翻垃圾堆。

而也就是在这一天，极光出现了。
极光带走了她，为她提供了衣食住行，给她能饱腹的食物，还教她识字，学习魔法。
所以，当极光领了新的任务回来，珂赛特满眼期待地看着她。
“有什么是我能帮上忙的吗？无论什么任务，我都会尽全力去做的！”
极光满脸复杂的表情，最后叹了口气。
“那你就跟我去诺瓦大陆吧，作为「冬眠者」，混入诺瓦人的社会，潜伏到我传唤你为止。”
“不过在那之前，你得先学会隐藏角的魔法。”
珂赛特信心满满。
“我一定顺利完成任务！极光大人！”

从拜雅到诺瓦大陆的过程，珂赛特有些记不清了，也许是太兴奋了，也许是太紧张了。回过神的时候，他们这一批「冬眠者」已经攀上绝壁的瀑布，来到了树木茂密的森林。
珂赛特站在这片土地上，映入眼中的绿色像是生命力的具象化，微风习习，虫鸣与鸟啼合奏­——那是拜雅见不到的景象。
她又抬头看了一眼身后的瀑布，奔腾的水流飞跃而下，流向不可见的深处。
原来诺瓦的世界，是这样子的。
珂赛特静静地站了一会，然后背起行囊，根据地图指引和任务目标，走向一个全新的冒险。

CharacterArchiveContent.14213.2.en:
"So hungry... Will I be able to find food today?" she thought.
In the night sky, a full moon hanging high, casting silver light over the ruined village. There was little sign of life in sight.
"Days ago, a house on the back side of the village collapsed."
Cosette, light-headed from hunger, vaguely remembered a group of beggars talking about it earlier that day. She thought about it briefly: there might still be food left in the building. Maybe she could find something within the ruins...
Thus she gathered her energy and headed toward the north of the village.
Unfortunately, her hope was quickly dashed. It was a small village, and by the time Cosette arrived at the collapsed house, it had already been thoroughly searched. Forget food—even corpses might have already been cleared away.
She sighed, sat down by the crumbled walls, letting out another long, heavy sigh. She hadn't found anything to eat in the last two days. A loud growl from her belly echoed in the silence of the night.

"Hey, are you hungry?"
A lively voice came from behind her. Cosette quickly lifted her head to find another dirty, scruffy girl perched on a half-broken wall, staring down at her.
"Your stomach's growling so loud. If you're that hungry... Here, take this."
The girl rummaged through her equally filthy pack and pulls out two flatbreads, handing them to Cosette. They were dry and hard, no telling how long they've been kept.
Cosette froze for a second. Then instinct took over because survival came first. She devoured one of the flatbreads in just a few bites, nearly choking on the rock-hard crust.
The girl laughed at the sight of her scarfing everything down, then handed her a water bag. Seeing how young Cosette was, she eventually gave her two more small bread rolls.
"Keep them. This village is almost deserted. Before you go hungry again, you'd better move on."
"If I take your food... What about you?"
"I'll meet up with my partner before dawn, so don't worry about me... Don't look at me like that. I can't take you with me. We're about to do something dangerous. Might even die."
"Eh?"
The girl pointed up at the sky. The moonlight bathed her in a shimmering glow.
"They say in the sky there's a paradise, with clean water and endless food. If we can find it, maybe we'll never have to starve again."
"But how could people ever reach the sky?"
The girl didn't answer. When she left, she told Cosette that she hoped someday Cosette could leave this wretched place behind.

The encounter with the girl was but a brief interlude in Cosette's life. Cosette's good fortune did not last.
She didn't manage to leave the decaying village before the next hunger struck. And the next day, her bread rolls were taken by other hungry kids in the village.
In a place like this, there were all too many orphans like her.

"If... if I couldn't even hold onto the kindness that others showed me, then how could I ever repay them...?"
The setting sun stretched her shadow long and crooked across the trash piles.
At that moment, she spotted a metal object half-buried under garbage bags. She stared at it for a long time before finally dragging it out with effort.
—It was a steel claw.
Too large and too heavy for the girl as she was then. Yet, as if guided by fate, she wiped the grime away. In the last light of sunset, she dragged it with both hands and walked out of the dump.
If she had a weapon—if she had strength—then one day...
CharacterArchiveContent.14213.2.cn:
好饿……今天能找到食物吗……
圆月高挂，银白的月光撒在这个破败的村庄里，放眼望去看不到一丝生机。
前几天似乎村子北面好像有个房子倒塌了。
珂赛特饿得发晕，隐约记得今天似乎有流浪汉在讨论这件事。她短暂地思考了一下，有建筑或许就会有食物，或许能在废墟里翻出点什么……
她想着，打起精神往村子北边走去。
只可惜希望很快落空。村子不大，珂赛特找到那个倒塌的房子时，那堆废墟已经被人翻了个地朝天，看上去别说食物了，就算是尸体，说不定也已经被清理干净了。
女孩叹了口气，在残垣断壁边坐下，长长地叹了口气。她已经两天没找到东西吃了，肚子饿得咕咕响，在这个寂静的夜里显得格外明显……

“嘿，你饿了吗？”
一个飒爽的声音在她背后响起。女孩猛地抬起头，一个跟她一样脏兮兮的少女趴在那半截断墙上，正低头看着她。
“你肚子叫得好大声哦，饿了的话……喏，这个给你吃吧。”
少女从她那个同样脏兮兮的行囊里翻出来两块烧饼，递到珂赛特的手里——干巴巴的，也不知道放了多久。
珂赛特愣了一下，下一秒本能已经占据上风，她不顾上别的，生存的第一任务似乎只剩下吃，三五下就啃完了一个烧饼，还差点被着硬邦邦的面食噎住。
少女看着她狼吞虎咽的样子直笑，又拿过水袋给她，最后或许是看珂赛特年纪小，又掏出两个小面包给她。
“拿着吧，这个村子已经快没人了，在下次饿肚子之前，赶紧换个地方。”
“这些给我的话，那你……”
“我天亮前会跟我伙伴汇合，所以别担心……别那样看着我，我带不了你，我们正准备去做一件冒险的事情，搞不好会死的。”
“欸？”
月光下，少女指了指天上。
“听说天空之上存在一个乐园，那里有干净的水源，又充足的食物，如果我们找到那个乐园，说不定就不用再挨饿了。”
“但人怎能到天上去呢？”
少女没有回答，只是在分别的时候，真挚地祝福珂赛特，希望她有一天也能离开这个糟糕的地方。

少女的出现终究只是一个插曲，好运对珂赛特来说并不是持续的。
她并没有在下次饿肚子之前走出这个破败的村子，甚至，少女留给她的那点食物，也在隔天被其他流浪的孩子抢走。
在这个地方，像她这样的孤儿太多了。

“如果……如果连别人施舍给我的善意都无法守护的话，那又要如何回报呢……”
夕阳把她的影子拉得细长，歪歪扭扭地铺在垃圾堆上。
就在这一刹那，女孩低头看到了一个被垃圾袋压在底部的金属物件，她盯着那个金属物件看了很久，最终费劲地将它拖了出来。
——那是一个钢爪。
无论是大小还是重量，对现在的女孩来说都不适配。但像是福至心灵，女孩努力地擦去钢爪上的污渍，在夕阳最后的余晖里，拖着这个东西离开了垃圾场。
只要有武器的话，只要有力量的话，总有一天……

直率，认真，效率，以及，稍微有一些“个性”。这是大多数旅人们对于风影的评价。
当被问起为什么身为黎明近卫却总是和旅人走得很近时，她承认确实是为了在民间获得更多的关于永夜的情报，但即便如此，大家还是愿意将信任托付给她。

CharacterArchiveContent.14310.2.en:
The Anti-Nocturn-Eterna Ace

Combat simulations reveal that Wraith anticipates events two seconds before they happen. This isn't magic. It's a "superpower" forged from relentless training, acute observation, and god-like reflexes.
This ability gives her a massive edge against the unknown, making her our best asset against the Nocturn Eterna.
— Combat Evaluation Division, Sentinel of Dawn
CharacterArchiveContent.14310.2.cn:
对永夜的王牌

在模拟战中，我们惊讶地发现，在战斗中的风影具备看见两秒后的未来。这并非是天赋，而是依靠千锤百炼的武艺和对万事万物细致入微的观察，以及极快的反应力所能达到的类似“超能力”的境界。
凭借这份能力，在对抗未知的敌人，尤其是永夜时，能发挥出最大的优势。
——黎明近卫 战斗评测部门

CharacterArchiveContent.14311.2.en:
Wraith wanders the streets of the City of a Thousand Monoliths, fresh off a commission and mulling over how to "reward" herself.
She doesn't really "get" leisure. She is simply mimicking the traditions of her clan: the post-hunt feast. Back home, food is an offering to comrades, family, and glory.
But here, all Wraith can manage is a small, symbolic gesture.
"Hey, look. It's Wraith."
"She must be on a job. I wonder who could possibly order someone like her around."
Wraith ignores the whispers trailing her. She has dealt with these staring eyes since the day she arrived in the city.
Still, their gossip triggers a memory—her very first "commission" here.

Back then, she was a stranger plagued by bizarre rumors and suspicious glares. Worse, she was constantly worrying about where her next meal would come from.
Trust is currency among Trekkers, and a foreign face has no value. The city air felt more suffocating than any northern blizzard, and sure enough, she couldn't land a single job.
Just as she was contemplating a grim future, a girl's cry pierced the air. Wraith looked up to see a red balloon drifting skyward.
Instinct took over. She scaled the wall in a blur, leaped from the roof, and snatched the balloon mid-air. The crowd below applauded, assuming it was a street performance.
Before the girl could even react, this silver-haired stranger was already standing in front of her, balloon in hand.

"Here. Don't lose it again. Bye."
"Please wait!"
The girl stopped her, offering a thank-you gift: a round, white dessert.
"What is this? White... Cold... Is it snow?"
"It's ice cream! I'm out of allowance money, but please take this. Thanks for saving my balloon."
"My apologies, but I haven't fallen low enough to eat ice and snow. In my homeland, only a failed hunter would resort to eating..."
"You... You don't like it? I-I'm sorry..."
"Ugh, no! I didn't mean that! Don't cry! Look, I'm eating it, okay?"
Wraith took a cautious bite. Beyond the nostalgic chill, a rich, creamy sweetness flooded her mouth. A faint flush rose on her cheeks.
"This! What is this? It's so sweet... Is the local 'snow' always like this?"
"I told you, it's called ice cream! But I'm glad you like it."
"Thank you. I have never seen anything this magical back home. I will remember its name."
"Um... Can I have another one?"
"Wow, you really love ice cream. Alright, I'll tell you a secret..."

"Miss? Have you decided on your order?"
The server's question snaps her back to reality. Without realizing it, her search for a "reward" has led her straight to this familiar shop.
"I'll take one Ultra-Creamy Double-Nut Supreme Cross-Star Special, please."
Ignoring the stares around her, Wraith places her order with absolute confidence.
"I never expected anyone to actually order the secret menu item... Ahaha..."
"It was the first magic spell I learned in this city."
"And I ... really like it."
CharacterArchiveContent.14311.2.cn:
风影走在千塔之城的街道上，刚完成一场委托的她正思考如何给自己一份“嘉奖”。
其实她并不懂生活，这么做的目的也只不过是模仿故乡的家族习惯——人们总会在狩猎后设宴欢庆。为战友，为家人，为荣耀献上美食。
只是在这里，风影只能象征性地给自己一点小小的奖励。
“喂，你快看，是那个风影啊。”
“一定是来这里做委托的吧，真不知道什么样的人才能使唤她去做事。”
风影没有理睬身后旅人们的窃窃私语，毕竟这样的经历从她刚踏入这座城市就已经开始了。
只是旅人们的对话，让她回想起了在这的“第一份委托”。

那是的她初来乍到，被异样的目光审视，被奇怪的传言侵扰，那时的她还需要为温饱而考虑。
旅人社群讲究信用，完全陌生的面孔自然与这个词相性不佳。比起北方的风雪，这里的氛围更令她喘不过气——果不其然，她并没能接到任何一份委托。
正当她为自己的未来而犯愁时，却见一个女孩对着天空哭喊，视线望去，一颗红色的气球升向了高空。
风影本能地行动起来，她扶墙而上，眨眼间便来到了楼顶，随着纵身一跃，在无数人的目光下抓住了那个红色的气球。人们只当是一场即兴表演为她而鼓掌。
女孩还没反应过来，一位银白长发的异国女子便牵着气球来到她跟前。

“给，不要弄丢了。再见。”
“等一下姐姐！”
女孩叫住风影并递来了她的谢礼，那是一个白色的球形甜品。
“这是什么？白色的，冰凉凉，是雪吗？”
“是雪糕啦姐姐，我没零花钱，但这个可以给你。谢谢你帮我拿回了气球。”
“抱歉，还没惨到需要吃这个的地步，在我的故乡，只有非常失败的猎人才会吃……”
“你不喜欢吗……？对，对不起……”
“呃！不是，我，我不是这个意思！别哭，我吃总可以了吧！”
风影接过小女孩递来的雪糕，轻轻咬上一口，除了那份令人怀念的温度，随之蔓延开的还有一股浓郁的奶香。她的脸颊也泛起细微的红晕。
“这！这是什么？好甜……这就是千塔之城的雪吗？”
“都说它叫雪糕啦，不过姐姐你喜欢就行。”
“谢谢你，在我的家乡还从来没见过这么神奇的东西，我会记住它的名字的。”
“那个……我能再要一个吗？”
“姐姐你真的好喜欢雪糕啊，真没办法，告诉你一个秘诀好了。其实……”

“这位客人，决定好点什么了吗？”
服务员的询问将她的思绪拉回，思考着怎么奖励自己的风影不自觉得便来到熟悉的店铺前。
“请给我来一份’浓郁奶香坚果加倍双层夹心闪耀至尊十字星雪糕’。”
不在意周围的目光，风影自信地如此回答道。
“没想到，真的会有人点这个隐藏款呢~啊哈哈……”
“这是我来到这里后学会的第一个的魔法。”
“我，真的很喜欢。”

CharacterArchiveContent.14312.2.en:
Familiar faces crowded the plaza. Putting aside the fresh grief of lost homes and kin, the people gathered to witness a warrior's birth.
A young girl emerged from the crowd. Under the community's gaze, the Council pinned a medal of honor to her chest. Her mission: to scale the perilous Behemoth Mountains alone, crossing a deadly frontier to reach the continent's heart.
A few days ago, she overheard a conversation between the messengers of the Grace Imperium and the councilors: this tragedy was no natural disaster—it was a deliberate act of man.
To uncover the truth, she must journey to the City of a Thousand Monoliths and find the very source of all this suffering.
"May your soul return to glory."
The clan chanted their highest blessing in unison before returning to the grim work of rebuilding.

"May your soul return to glory..."
The girl murmured the words, drifting awake. Outside, a blizzard howled, reminding her she was still at the summit of the Behemoth Mountains. Half a year had already vanished into the snow.
"... Out of rations."
She couldn't afford to sleep. In this demonic realm that had claimed countless warriors, she had to fight for every scrap of survival.
By dim candlelight, she unrolled a map. Her finger traced a handwritten note pointing to a crevice in the peaks—a rumored pass leading out of the snow and into the interior of Nova.
A dull ache flared in her side. That was a "souvenir" from a recent battle with an Icefang Beast. She had wanted to claim its fang as a trophy, but the ice beneath her cracked. Faced with a choice, she resolutely chose life.
"Coming home empty-handed is usually a joke, but luckily, under the circumstances..."
She applied the last of her salve to the wound.
A shadow darted across the dark rock wall. Reflexes took over as she snatched a rock lizard from a crevice.
"... I can't go back. And I don't need to."
With a quick snap, she ended it. She struck a flint and prepared her first meal in two days.
"Thank you. Your life won't be wasted."
After cleaning up, she added another mark to her travel log.

Time blurred. When she finally came to, the hard ice underfoot had given way to soft, damp soil. Smoke rose gently from chimneys on the horizon.
Trekkers passed by in groups, glancing curiously at her, then adjusted their packs and continued toward the distant Monolith.
She stopped at a stream to wash away the grime. Fish darted playfully around her ankles. She studied her reflection: silver-white hair falling past her ears. It seemed the only thing consistent was that color of home.
It finally hit her: she had come a very long way.
CharacterArchiveContent.14312.2.cn:
熟悉的人们聚在广场的中央，他们暂时抛下刚失去家园，失去亲人的悲伤，站在这里是为了见证新一位战士的诞生。
一个女孩从人群中走来，在众人的目光下，被议会授予荣誉的勋章，她将独自攀登北方最为凶险的巨兽山脉，穿过鲜有人到达的险境直达大陆的中部。
女孩在数天前听见了恩赐意志的使者们同议员的谈话——这场悲剧并非是天灾，而是人祸。
想要得知那份真相，她只能亲自前往千塔之城，找到一切苦难的源头。
“愿你的灵魂，归于荣耀。”
人们齐声，向出发的少女献上家族最敬重的祝福，然后，又回到重建家园的忙碌中了。

“愿你的灵魂，归于荣耀……”
女孩呢喃着，渐渐醒了过来。洞穴外呼啸的风雪提醒她已经来到了巨兽山脉之巅，转眼间，这趟旅程也走过了近半年之久。
“食物……见底了啊。”
她不能就这样轻易睡去，在这片困住了无数战士的魔境里，她必须竭尽全力寻找新的生机。
铺开地图，借着微弱的烛光，手指顺着黑色笔记的方向落在了群山间的缝隙——据说在这里隐藏着能走出雪山，向着诺瓦内陆前进的通路。
正这么想着，侧腹传来隐隐的痛觉，那是前不久她战胜一只冰牙兽时留下的“勋章”。她本想将这份荣耀和战利品收入囊中，却不料脚下的冰层极速断裂，在两难的取舍间，她果断选择了活下去的那条路。
“出门狩猎空手而归可是会被笑话的，不过好在……”
她用光最后一点药膏，涂抹在受伤的地方。
余光间，她瞥见黑暗的岩壁间闪过一只小小的身影，她眼疾手快，将对方从石缝间拽了出来——是一只岩壁蜥蜴。
“已经回不去，也没有必要回去了……”
她稍作用力，以最利落地方式结束了眼前的生命，又迅速生起火焰，开始料理她两天里唯一获得的食物。
“谢谢，我不会浪费你给予的生命。”
简单收拾完后，她在记录行程的册子上又划上一笔。
 
不知又过了多久，回过神来，脚下的坚冰已变为柔软湿润的泥土，远方的地平线也缓缓升起了几缕炊烟。
结伴而行的旅人们从对面走来，只是打量了她一会，又挑着行李，朝远方的星塔走去。
她来到一处小河边清洗身上的污垢，鱼虾欢快地在她的脚边游动，望着水中的倒影，银白长发顺着耳尖垂落，不变的，似乎只有那抹故乡的颜色。
此时她终于意识到，自己，已经走了很远了。

CharacterArchiveContent.14313.2.en:
Silence hung over the quiet cemetery on the Silver District outskirts of the City of a Thousand Monolith.
The old gravekeeper was up with the sun, as always. Washed and dressed, he headed out to sweep the fallen leaves.
Nearby, a white-haired girl stood before a fresh headstone, clutching a bouquet.
She wore a solemn expression in her formal black, looking like she had just bade goodbye to an old friend.
"Did they ... have a good life?"
The old man had seen this scene a thousand times. The words of comfort came automatically.
"Served my grandfather, scaled snowy peaks, fought off monsters... Lived a life of glory."
"Grandfather introduced us. We were partners until the end, sworn to crush every villain we met."
"Sounds like a warrior worth respecting."
"We were chasing a Nocturn Eterna recently. It took a direct magic hit... Critical damage to its lever-action mechanism."
"I struggled for a long time, but I've decided to bring it back."
"My condolences... Wait, what?"

Wraith placed a can of gun oil on the grave.
"I used to be able to cock it one-handed. Learned that trick from a Stella Drama."
"After the battle, I rebuilt it. Even fused it with parts from one of my melee weapons."
"Shame I can't do that cool reload flip anymore, though."
As Wraith spoke, she lifted her "resurrected" comrade from its case.
"It used to be 'Blizzard 987,' after the Monolith Year it was summoned."
"Now, it has a new name: Bayonet Zero Alter."
"Alright. Say goodbye to the old you, partner."
Wraith stood and walked over to the old man.
"Thanks, sir. Weird as it sounds, you're the first person who didn't slip off as I told my story."
"Let's go, partner. Time to find those guys and get the revenge."

The old man stared at her retreating back, speechless, before finally muttering under his breath.
"Kids these days are intense ... in every sense of the word."
CharacterArchiveContent.14313.2.cn:
千塔银城区的郊外，一片宁静的墓园中。
老守墓人向往常一样早早得起了床，简单洗漱后来到墓园里清扫落叶。
不远处，白发的姑娘正捧着束鲜花站在一块新的石碑旁。
她身着黑礼服，神情庄重，似乎刚与一位老友道别。
“他……生前过得如何？”
老人见过太多这样的情景，不自觉地向白发姑娘搭话。
“跟过我爷爷，爬上过雪山，对付过魔兽，一生都活在荣耀里。”
“爷爷把它介绍给我，直到不久前，它还是我最好的搭档，我们发誓要击溃所有恶人。”
“是个受人尊敬的战士啊。”
“前不久，我们在追击一个永夜成员的时候，它被魔法击中，杠杆机关受损严重……”
“我做了很久的心理建设，终于决定让他复活。”
“令人惋惜……嗯？”

风影在墓碑前递上一罐保养枪械用油。
“曾经我可以用他单手上膛，这还是我从一部影戏里学到的。”
“那次战斗后，我对他进行了重组，把他和我的另一把近身用武装融合在了一起。”
“只可惜，再也用不了那帅气的上膛方式了。”
风影说着，将那位“复活”的战友从箱子里取了出来。
“过去他叫’风雪987’，是为了纪念它在星塔历987年首次被许愿出来。”
“现在，他有了新的名字——零式枪刃·改”
“好了，和过去的自己道别吧，搭档。”
风影站起身，走到老人的身边。
“谢谢您，老先生。虽然这么说有些奇怪，但您还是第一个在我讲故事的途中没有借机开溜的人。”
“我们走吧搭档，该去找那些家伙给你报仇了。”

望着风影离开的背影，语塞了很久的老人小声嘀咕了一句。
“现在的年轻人真厉害啊……各种意义上。”

CharacterArchiveContent.14402.3.en: To become the sharpest blade in all of Nova with Boss as my Wielder
CharacterArchiveContent.14402.3.cn: 成为属于魔王的全诺瓦最锋利的刀

CharacterArchiveContent.14403.2.en:
The Basic Standard for a Wielder

One who is not harmed by my aura of edge.
CharacterArchiveContent.14403.2.cn:
持刀人的基本标准

不会被妾身周身的锐气所伤。

CharacterArchiveContent.14404.2.en:
Parents and Master

The twin blades on my back are "Father and Mother," while the odachi is "Master."
My own strength is still lacking, and I have yet to truly become a worthy blade. Thus I must still rely on their power.
CharacterArchiveContent.14404.2.cn:
父母与师

背上的两把太刀是「父上和母上」，而大太刀则是「师父」。
妾身的实力还不够，还未能彻底成为一把合格的刀，依旧需要借助他们的力量。

CharacterArchiveContent.14405.2.en:
Amekiku

A once-abandoned traveler's inn on the outskirts of the City of a Thousand Monoliths, later refurbished by Chitose into something resembling a dojo and given the name "Amekiku."
Chitose usually offers conveniences here to passing Trekkers, including but not limited to weather forecasts and tea service.
—From the words of Trekkers passing through
CharacterArchiveContent.14405.2.cn:
听雨

一座在千塔城郊附近的废弃旅人驿站，在千都世的一番整修之后被改造成了道馆的样子，并取名为“听雨”。
平日里，千都世会在这座驿站中为旅人们提供便利，包括但不限于天气预报、茶水服务。
——来自途径旅人的口述

CharacterArchiveContent.14406.2.en:
Treasure bag

Besides the three katanas she carries, Chitose's pack holds many other things, bundled together like a treasure bag. When opened, it can even serve as a quilt.
It holds: a set of blade maintenance tools, Chitose's daily necessities, a change of clothes, a cloth bag for rice balls, and more.

"Even in the Wilds, one must not act with abandon; propriety, cleanliness, and restraint must never be neglected." —"Family Rites", Volume VI (excerpt)
CharacterArchiveContent.14406.2.cn:
百宝箱

千都世背上的行囊里除了三把太刀外，还像百宝箱一样裹着很多其他的东西，其本身打开后还可当做是一条被子。
行囊内的物品：一套保养刀具物品、一套千都世的生活用品、一套换洗的衣服、一个用来装饭团的布袋等等。

“即使身处荒野，亦不可肆意妄为；「礼」「净」「敛」皆不可松懈。” ——《家礼》第六卷（节选）

CharacterArchiveContent.14407.2.cn:
刀的保养

首先取下刀柄，分离刀身；
然后用干净布擦拭刀身，去除旧油与灰尘；
随后用蘸有刀油的布均匀涂抹刀身，避免生锈；
最后将刀收入鞘中，切记不可放于潮湿之处。
此为每日必做之事。

Shuriken Charm

A charm marked with a shuriken pattern, which Chitose has always worn at her waist as a family heirloom.
CharacterArchiveContent.14410.2.cn:
手里剑御守

一枚印有手里剑花纹的御守，千都世一直将其作为家族的传家宝佩戴在腰间。

CharacterArchiveContent.14411.2.en:
It is said that in the distant past, a terrifying "Oni" once ruled over Windhowl Island.
It could peer into human hearts, control their will, and force the people of Matsukawa City to climb the Monolith and offer up their memories as sacrifice.
Time and again, the islanders chose brave warriors to slay the Oni, but because it could sense all hostility, every challenger was killed before they could act.
At last, a swordswoman named Matsuko proposed a plan called "the human blade": to temper someone into a being without love, without hate, without heart—thus becoming a pure "blade" that the Oni could not perceive.
This heartless Blade, stripped of all emotion and distraction, possessed only the will to cut; its speed was nearly divine.
Yet, though the Blade was sharp, it could not choose its target on its own. It needed a "Wielder" to guide where the edge would fall.
Only when the Blade and its Wielder became of one mind, reaching the state of "Jinken Hitotsu," could the Blade sense the Wielder's intent and act without command.
In the end, only a single pair ever achieved this Oneness—and they succeeded in destroying the Oni.
From then on, the tradition of "human blade" endured in that land, and families tied to it flourished for a time.
But never again did anyone reach that supreme state of Oneness, and so those families declined, leaving only whispers of the tale carried on the wind.
CharacterArchiveContent.14411.2.cn:
相传，遥远的过去，风息岛上曾经盘踞着一只可怖的恶鬼。
它能窥探人心，操控意志，迫使松川城的居民攀上星塔，献祭记忆。
岛民屡次选拔勇者讨伐恶鬼，却因恶鬼能感知一切敌意，将勇者悉数扼杀于行动之前。
直到一位名叫松子的剑士提出了一项名叫“以人为刀”的计划，即将人淬炼成无爱无恨无心的刀，如此方能避开恶鬼的感知。
无心的刀摒弃了情感与杂念，仅存纯粹的斩击意志，其刀速之快，几近神技。
但刀虽凌厉，却无法自行锁定目标，需由持刀人指引刀刃挥动的方向。
唯有当刀与持刀人心意相通，达到“人刀合一”之境，刀方能感知持刀人的思绪，无需指令便可自主行动。
最终，只有一对搭档达到了此般的境界，并成功诛灭恶鬼。
此后，“以人为刀”的传统在当地延续，并令当地的家族盛极一时。
然而，再无人能重现“人刀合一”的至高境界，家族亦随之没落，只余传说在风中低语。

CharacterArchiveContent.14412.2.en:
"Wow, it's really coming down!"
"There's a pavilion over there! Let's get out of all this rain for a bit!"

On Nova, during Tonitrua Month, the weather could turn in an instant. Clear skies in the morning, but by noon the clouds rolled in, and before long a torrential downpour left Trekkers drenched from head to toe.

"Sorry... Hope we're not intruding..."
Two Trekkers darted into the pavilion, and there they found a young girl quietly polishing her blade.
"Not at all. This pavilion was built as a shelter for Trekkers from both wind and rain."
She rose, poured two cups of hot tea from a small kettle, and offered them to the visitors.

"Thank you so much!"
The Trekkers accepted gratefully, thanking her again and again.
She only gave a small nod before settling back into the corner, wiping her blade once more.

"Master, do you think we can still make it to Philae on time?"
"If the rain stops before sundown, we should."
"So ... We'll have to travel by night?"
"Yes. If this letter isn't delivered on time, the pay will be halved."
The older Trekker frowned at the sheets of rain outside, silently praying for it to ease.

Not long after, the storm seemed to let up, and the misty mountains came back into view.
"Come on, let's go!"
The older Trekker urged, quickly packing up.

"The rain hasn't truly stopped. It'll likely go on for another two or three days."
The girl set her blade down and looked at them.
"How can you tell?"
"If that's true, then we need to leave right now!"
But the moment one of them stepped outside, the rain came crashing down again. Raindrops as big as beans pelted the flagstones, splashing up bursts of spray.
The Trekkers froze, looking back at the girl.

"Even so, I would not recommend traveling in this weather."
"Why not?"
"To reach Philae you must cross the mountains. In rain like this, the roads grow muddy and the slopes become treacherous. There will be dangers unseen."
The Trekkers studied her—At her side there was no rain gear, as if in this fickle season she had no fear at all of being suddenly soaked by the rain.

"There will be strong winds tonight. If you turn back now and explain things to your client, they might be understanding."
Her gaze stayed fixed on the distant peaks, calm and certain.

"We shall go back."
"Master? Back to where?"
"Back to where we come from."
Rumor has it that on the outskirts of the City of a Thousand Monoliths, there stands an inn called Amekiku.
If the girl inside says rain is coming, the skies will open without fail. If she says the winds will rise, then the mountains will surely howl.
CharacterArchiveContent.14412.2.cn:
“哇！好大的雨啊！”
“那边有个亭子！我们去那里避一避吧！”

雷月的诺瓦大陆天气总是变幻莫测，或许早上还是晴空万里，到了中午便会乌云密布，转眼间暴雨倾盆，将毫无防备的旅人浇得浑身湿透。

“对不起……打扰了……”
两位旅人匆匆躲进亭中，发现一位少女正静静擦拭着手中的刀剑。
“无妨，这亭子本就是为旅人遮风避雨而建。”
少女起身，从茶炉上斟了两杯热茶递去。

“多谢！”
旅人接过茶杯，并不断的向少女表达着感激。
少女只是微微颔首，便坐回角落，继续擦拭她的刀刃。

“师父，我们还能按时赶到菲莱吗？”
“如果雨能在太阳落山前停止，应该就可以。”
“要……赶夜路吗？”
“嗯，如果这封信件没有按时送达的话，报酬就会少一半。”
年长的旅人望着亭外密布的雨幕，眉头紧锁，祈祷着雨能快一些停止。

没一会，雨便逐渐停了下来，雾蒙蒙的群山也变得清晰可见。
“快！走了！”
年长旅人催促着，收拾起了行囊。

“雨并未停歇，可能还会持续两三天。”
少女放下了手中的刀剑，看向旅人。
“你怎么知道？”
“如果这样的话，我们现在就应该立刻上路！”
话未说完，刚踏出亭外的旅人便被重新倾泻的暴雨逼退。豆大的雨点砸在青石板上，溅起水花。
旅人一时愣在了原地，看向这位少女。

“即便如此，妾身更不建议你们冒雨赶路。”
“为什么？”
“去往菲莱需翻越群山，暴雨之下山路泥泞湿滑，更有未知之险。”
旅人打量着眼前少女——少女身旁并无雨具，仿佛在这样阴晴不定的月份中，她并不会害怕突然的降雨将自己淋湿。

“今晚还会有大风，若现在折返，向委托人说明缘由，或许还能挽回。”
少女她望向远处，眼中无半分犹疑。

“我们回了。”
“师父？回哪？”
“千塔。”
相传，在千塔城郊有一座名叫“听雨”的亭子。
若亭中少女言雨将至，雨必倾盆；若她说风欲起，风必呼啸。

CharacterArchiveContent.14413.1.en: Weapon Anecdote: Her Majesty the Blade

CharacterArchiveContent.14413.2.en:
"Remember, the highest form of swordsmanship is a mind as still as water, occupied by nothing but the cut."
"Understood, Master."
"Then... Again."
With that, the girl slowly slid her blade back into its scabbard and closed her eyes. For an instant, time itself seemed to stand still.
"Ha!—"
No one could say exactly when the sword had left its scabbard. A flash of white light tore through the air, leaving a cross-shaped afterimage ahead.
To the onlookers, it looked as if she had swung only once, but in truth she had delivered two strikes.
Without the aid of magic, to unleash such speed with nothing but flesh and bone was already the very limit of human capability.
And yet—
"Not enough! Still not fast enough!"
"Master..."
"That's enough for today."
The girl quietly picked up the odachi beside her. She traced her fingertips along its edge before she wiped it clean and carefully set it back on the rack.
"Are we really going to keep up this charade, my lord?"
A faint voice drifted from a small room beside the dojo.
"It has been years, and she still can't perform that legendary strike! Was the legend nothing but a lie?"
"Then...?"
"Starting tomorrow, remove all the servants from this hall."
"Even her 'parents'?"
"I am her 'Master', and I shall no longer be here. Do you really think there's any need to keep the 'parents?'"
"As you command."
From that day on, the girl kept watch over the ever-emptier dojo alone. Her "parents" and "master" never show up again. Her world became nothing but the daily rhythm of sword practice and study.
Years passed. The roof of the hall began to leak; the wooden floors slowly rotted away.
Until one dawn, when the dew was still fresh, she caught her reflection on the cold steel as she wiped her blade—the silence of her "parents" and "master" had not been punishment for her lack of improvements. Instead, they had already become the "blade" in her hands.
At last, in the morning fog, the girl shouldered her pack and walked away, disappearing into the distance. She was setting out to find the one person spoken of in legend, the "Wielder" who could make her truly become the Blade.
CharacterArchiveContent.14413.2.cn:
“记住，剑道之极，唯有心如止水，一味的劈斩。”
“明白，师父。”
“那么，再试一次。”
说罢，少女缓缓收刀入鞘，双眸轻阖。刹那间，时间仿佛凝滞。
“哈——”
不知何时刀已从刀鞘中拔出，只见一道白色刀光划破空气，在前方留下十字形的残影。
旁观者眼中，少女似乎只挥了一刀，但实则完成了两次斩击。
无需魔法加持，仅凭血肉之躯挥出如此神速，已是凡人所能企及的极限。
然而——
“不够！还是不够快！”
“师父……”
“今日就到这里。”
少女默默捧起一旁的大太刀，指尖拂过刀身，在将其擦拭干净后小心翼翼的放在了刀架上。
“这样的把戏还要继续吗？主公大人。”
道馆一旁的小房间里传出了细微的声音。
“这都几年了，依然使不出来传说中的那一招！难道传说是骗人的吗？”
“那接下来……”
“从明天开始，撤走道馆里所有的仆人。”
“包括她的「父母」吗？”
“我这个「师父」都不在了，你觉得「父母」还有必要留着吗？”
“遵命。”
自那日起，少女便独自守着日渐冷清的道场。「父母」与「师父」再未与她交谈，她的世界只剩下日复一日的挥刀与读书。
岁月流逝，道场的屋檐开始漏雨，木地板也渐渐腐朽。
直到某个的晨露未干的黎明，她擦拭刀身时，忽然在冷铁上看见了自己的倒影——「父母」与「师父」的沉默并非是对自己剑术停滞的惩罚，而是早已化作她手中的刀。
终于，在晨雾中，少女背起行囊，身影渐行渐远，她要去寻找那个传说中能让自己成为“刀”的“持刀人”。

CharacterArchiveContent.14511.2.en:
Otoha had long forgotten exactly when she first left Windhowl Island for the mainland.
Her memories were hazy: the leader barking orders, hastily packing her bags, and trudging through the mud to board the ship. She remembered squeezing into the sweltering, packed lower deck before finally crossing the ocean to the other land.
The sun was shining brightly when she finally stepped ashore. She didn't cast a lingering gaze back at her homeland, like some ninjas romanticized in their journals. Instead, she just let the crowd jostle her forward, pulling her bamboo hat low to avoid drawing the guards' attention.
"There was no room for sentimentality in a situation like that," Otoha remarked. "I just wanted to survive."
She was undoubtedly lucky. Before the very next ship could even dock, a massive riot broke out on board. Rumors blamed it on an uneven split of loot or sudden betrayals, but either way, they all died right at the gates of the new world. The raging sea swallowed both their greed and their gold. That day, the sand frothed with dark red bubbles beneath everyone's feet—though it only took a few tides to wash the beach completely clean.

During those early days, Otoha drifted between cheap inns with her comrades. What remained of their organization was like a ship with a snapped mast; no one knew if it would ever sail again. As an ordinary mid-level ninja, she had no access to the higher-ups, let alone any clue about their grand schemes.
"Who are we taking revenge on? When will we ever get to go home?"
Her fellow travelers dwindled. Many found steady jobs or started families with locals. Perhaps that was the real point of crossing the ocean. For the first time, Otoha realized that even the most ironclad rules could crumble. The organization was so starved for cash that anyone wanting out could simply buy their freedom with a few large Dorra bills.
Faced with reality, all that talk of dignity, honor, and secrecy felt incredibly hollow.

She went through the most surreal period of her life: no missions, no danger. She often wandered aimlessly around this unfamiliar land. Once, she even spotted in a crowd the noble responsible for the ninjas' exile. He was wearing a sharply tailored suit, his face beaming as he followed a man in a black bird-head cloak into a carriage. He was living the good life.
She replayed that moment in her head countless times afterward, mapping out dozens of ways she could have assassinated him right then and there.
But she hadn't been given the order, so she couldn't act.
That night, she walked down to the beach, slid a dagger from her sleeve, and stared at it in the moonlight for a long time.
Then, with a forceful swing, she hurled the blade into the sea—dropping an anchor to steady her life in a crumbling world.

Years later, on certain nights, she still thought about that discarded blade. Maybe it had long since sunk to the ocean floor, or maybe a storm had washed it ashore, straight into the hands of some drifter trying their luck by the sea.
Her own fate remained inextricably tied to that dagger, rising and falling with the tides.
CharacterArchiveContent.14511.2.cn:
第一次从风息岛来到主大陆上，究竟是什么时候，乙叶已经不记得了。
在她模糊的印象中，自己被小首领叫着，仓促收拾好行李，踩着泥水踏上甲板，钻到闷热拥挤的底层船舱里，而后跨过大海，来到彼岸。
再踏上陆地时倒是阳光灿烂，她没有像一些颇有文学造诣的忍者在手记里记载的那样，回头再望一眼家乡的方向，而是被人群推搡着，紧紧下压斗笠以免被守卫发现异常。
“在那种情况下，根本没有什么伤感的情绪，只想着要找办法活下去。”——乙叶如此评价道。
她无疑是幸运的，下一班船还未靠岸，船上就爆发了巨大骚乱，流传的原因不外乎是分赃不均、有人叛变，最终一齐倒在了新世界的大门外。汹涌的海水吞没了财宝和欲望，那一天，人人脚下踩过的沙滩都冒着暗红的泡泡，而这一切也只需两三个夜晚浪潮便能冲刷干净。

最初的日子里，乙叶没有稳定的住所，和同伴们辗转于便宜的旅店。残余的组织像折断桅杆的破船，谁都不知道是否可以再次航行。她只是一个普通的中级忍者，接触不到上层的头目，不清楚他们的宏大计划。
“复仇的目标在哪里，重返家乡究竟要等到哪一天？”
同行者越来越少，不少人找了份稳定的工作，或是和当地人组建了新的家庭——原来这才是漂洋过海的真正意义。乙叶第一次知道，看似不可撼动的铁板规则也有松脱的那一天。由于资金过于匮乏，想要脱离组织的成员只需缴纳几张大面额朵拉便可除名。
一切尊严、荣誉、秘密在现实面前都尤为单薄。

她度过了迄今为止最不可思议的一段时光，没有任务，没有危险。她常常漫无目的地在这片陌生的土地闲逛，甚至有一次在人群里认出了导致忍者们流离失所的那位贵族头目。他换上了剪裁妥帖的西装，满脸堆笑，和一位身着鸟头黑披风的男人一前一后上了带篷马车——他过得好极了。
后来她无数次回想过当时的情景，一步步推演，设计出了数十种可以当场解决他的方法。
但她没有接到指示，她不能这样做。
那天晚上，她走到海边，从袖口里摸出一把短刀，借着月光端详了许久。
而后，她将短刀用力一挥，丢进大海，在她的人生与摇摇欲坠的世界钉下锚点。

多年后的一些夜晚，她常常回想起那把丢弃的短刀，它或许早已沉入深海，或许在某次风暴中席卷上岸，碰巧流入在海边碰运气的流浪者手中。
而她的命运始终与这把短刀牢牢捆绑在一起，沉浮与共。

CharacterArchiveContent.14512.2.en:
The first interview began on a drizzly autumn evening. As Otoha stopped in front of the café, a quick-handed server took her umbrella and held the door open. Across the scattering of customers, Otoha immediately spotted a slim figure. As if sensing her gaze, the figure suddenly turned, offering a smile—both surprised and restrained.

The rain whispered against the windows. The young girl leaned over the table, scribbling notes at a frantic pace, desperate not to miss a single detail, so excited that even her pen trembled slightly. Otoha waited silently. The dusk deepened, guests exchanged pleasantries as they left, and the café fell into a hush. A server stepped forward and lit a candle at their table.
She stared into the flame for a moment, then shyly asked:
"Excuse me... Do you... Do you happen to remember me?"
The young girl set down her pen, glancing up with curiosity at what seemed like an attempt to strike up a conversation.
"Hm?" Otoha tilted her head slightly. The server hesitated, realizing that the poised, elegant woman before her was nothing like the quiet junior she had once known.
"Sorry, my mistake. I thought you looked familiar at first, but upon a closer look... I must have been wrong."
Otoha smiled politely and gave a small nod, letting the awkward moment pass without a ripple.

The interview stretched on until closing time. The girl, thoroughly satisfied, snapped her notebook shut. That day's material would be enough to fuel several exciting novels. She thanked Otoha again:
"I can't believe you agreed to meet me. You're such a senior figure in the organization, and I'm just a nobody who never even liked training and only ever wanted to hide inside my room and write my stories."
"Ever since I learned about your story, I've always wanted to meet you. You are a bona fide legend..."
Otoha smiled and accepted the praise. She had merely carved out the tip of the iceberg from her past, added a little polish, and the girl accepted it as the full truth. And she remembered why she had agreed to the interview in the first place: the girl reminded her of her young apprentice—thin, stubborn, with the same wild and marvelous ideas swirling in her head.

After they said goodbye to each other, Otoha tightened her collar against the chill and walked toward the sea under the moonlight. She had once known this city like the back of her hand, yet now she found herself lost among the new buildings. It was like the server at the café—years ago, they had slept under the same low roof, but now they passed each other like strangers.
Her appearance had changed. Maybe someday, she thought, she wouldn't even recognize herself.

The last interview takes place the following spring. Otoha has received the organization's orders and is about to leave for her next assignment. As the interview ends, the girl gives her a deep bow. It's the highest gesture of respect among Goodwind ninjas.
"I'll turn your story into a biography. I am no great writer, but I want to record everything down."
"You're the most amazing ninja I've ever met. Even in the harshest conditions, you never gave up. You climbed all the way to where you are now..."
Otoha suddenly feels it wouldn't hurt to speak a little more honestly:
"I've read a few autobiographies before. People always cover up their flaws and mistakes, painting themselves as innocent victims of the world."
"Do you think I'm that kind of person?"
The girl stands frozen, turning Otoha's words over in her mind. Otoha gives her a small wave. It's time to go.

She turns away. The grass is fresh and green, the birdsong fading away, and the cherry blossoms have already fallen.
CharacterArchiveContent.14512.2.cn:
第一次访谈是在飘着细雨的深秋傍晚开始的。乙叶在咖啡厅前站定，眼疾手快的侍者接过雨伞，拉开大门。隔着零星几位客人，乙叶一眼就认出了那个瘦削的背影，而对方仿佛心有灵犀一般突然转过头，露出惊喜又克制的微笑。

雨声淅沥，年轻的女孩子俯在桌前飞快记录着，生怕漏掉任何一处细节，她甚至激动到笔尖都有些微微颤抖。乙叶默不作声地等待着，天色将晚，客人们寒暄着散去，咖啡厅没入夜色沉寂下来，侍者走上前，为她们点上蜡烛。
火光跃起的一瞬间，侍者出了神，而后怯怯地问道：
“不好意思，请问您……您还记得我吗？”
记录的女孩子放下笔，目光好奇地打探着这场看似搭讪的问话。
“嗯？”乙叶侧过脸，侍者怔了一下，确信眼前这位气质高贵的女人与记忆中那个沉默内敛的后辈绝非同一人。
“抱歉，抱歉，我只是觉得您有些面熟，但仔细一看……是我搞错了。”
乙叶依旧保持着微笑，微微一点头，一段小插曲平滑地结束了。

访谈一直持续到了咖啡厅打烊，女孩心满意足地合上笔记本，今日的素材足够她写出几篇激动人心的小说了，她再次向乙叶表达了感谢：
“我没想到您真的会答应我，毕竟您是组织里的大前辈，而我只是一个不务正业的小角色。我从小就不喜欢训练，只爱躲在房间里写小说。”
 “自从知道您的事迹之后，我一直想见您一面，您的经历称得上是传奇了……”
乙叶微笑着接受她的褒奖，她只是切出了过往的冰山一角，加之美化，眼前的女孩就信以为真。她想起了自己接受女孩访谈的缘由，女孩让她想到了自己的小徒弟。她们一样瘦弱、执着，脑子里装着和常人不一样的奇思妙想。

分别之后，乙叶裹紧衣领，沿着月光走向海边。以前她无比熟悉这座城邦，却也在新建的高楼前迷了路。就像咖啡馆的那位侍者，她们曾经睡在同一间低矮的平房里，多年后却对面不识。
她的容貌发生了一些改变，或许有一天她也会认不出自己。 

最后一次访谈是在第二年的春天，根据组织的指示，乙叶即将前往下一站。结束之后，女孩朝乙叶深深鞠了一躬，这是谷风忍者表达最高敬意的方式。
“我会将您的故事写成传记。虽然我的文笔很差，但还是希望能记录下这些。”
“您是我见过最厉害的忍者，在那么艰难的环境下都没有放弃，一步步走到了今天的位置……”
乙叶忽然觉得，这时候可以说几句无伤大雅的真心话了：
“我以前也看过一些人写的自传，他们总是悄悄隐去自身的缺陷与犯下的错误，把自己包装成一个清清白白、受到全世界迫害的可怜人。”
“你觉得我会是那样的人吗？”
女孩兀自愣在原地，思考着乙叶这番话的含义。乙叶朝女孩挥了挥手，她该走了。

她转身之后，草木新绿，鸟鸣渐息，樱花已经落了。

CharacterArchiveContent.14513.2.en:
"Heard the rumors? Some Trekker's been scouring the city for a weaponsmith."
"Yeah, I heard. Word is that her weapon specs are twenty pages long. One look and the smiths run for the hills. Then again, the payout she's offering is supposed to be just as insane."
"Makes you wonder what she's trying to build... I'm actually kind of curious."

Otoha stood at the fork in the road. She pulled out a scrawled map, double-checked her route, and headed down the narrow path to the right.
This was the seventh artisan she'd visited this month. Until now, every smith had politely turned her down the moment she handed over her weapon designs—even with her offering several times the going rate.
She wondered how long this one would even bother listening to her.
Swallowing her doubts, Otoha knocked on the door of the secluded cabin.

To her surprise, the elderly smith didn't flinch. When he took her twenty-three-page stack of weapon specs, his face actually lit up.
"I've been expecting you," the old man said, poring over the pages. "When I heard someone was waving around a ridiculous list of demands looking for a smith, I had to know who it was and what they were trying to make."
Otoha smiled to herself. At least she wasn't shown the door immediately this time.
"Then you've probably also heard that money is no object. I only care about one thing: is it actually possible to build this?"
"It looks complicated, but at the end of the day, you just want a gun. Am I right?"
"I don't care about its final shape. If you think it needs to be a gun, then it's a gun."
"I see. Fair enough."
The old man chuckled and handed the papers back. Otoha's heart sank. She thought this was another rejection, but then he walked over to his desk.
"These notes of yours are all over the place. Grab a seat. Let's figure out what this thing is actually going to look like."

...
One evening, two months later, Otoha formally thanked the smith and said her goodbyes. The old man just stared at the long parasol in her hands and sighed.
"We forge a barrel that beautiful, only for you to hide the whole thing under a parasol canopy."
Otoha had long since figured out the old man's quirks. "It needs to be hidden precisely because it's so beautiful."
"Hmph, you always have an answer for everything." The old man waved her off. "I just hope this weapon helps you accomplish whatever you've set out to do."
"It will. I promise you."
CharacterArchiveContent.14513.2.cn:
“你听说了吗？最近有个旅人在到处找能做武器的工匠。”
“啊听说了，据说她给出的武器要求足足有二十张纸，工匠们看了一眼就都吓跑了，不过那个旅人给出的佣金好像也高得离谱。”
“到底是想打造什么样的武器……都有点好奇了。”

乙叶站在岔路口，拿出那张潦草的手画地图，再三比对了路线，朝着右侧那条小路走去。
这是她这个月拜访的第七个工匠了，在这之前，每当她拿出她对这个武器构想的委托书时，接见她的工匠都委婉地拒绝了她的委托——哪怕她能给出超出寻常几倍的佣金。
也不知道今天这位工匠能听听她说多久。
怀抱着这一份不确定，乙叶敲开了工匠隐居的小木屋。

出乎意料的是，这位年龄不小的工匠在接过乙叶那份多达二十三页的武器构想和细节的委托书时，对方露出了欣喜的表情。
“我等你很久了。”老者仔细地翻看委托书，“听闻有个人拿着夸张的委托书在找打造武器的手艺人的时候，我就很好奇到底会是什么样的人，想要什么样的武器。”
乙叶暗暗窃喜，至少这次她不是被直接请出去。
“那您应该也听说了，这个委托的佣金不是问题，我只关心一件事，您觉得这个武器有可能造出来吗？”
“看上去很复杂，但核心诉求其实是一把枪，我说的对吗？”
“我对它的最终形态并没有要求，如果您觉得这应该是一把枪，那它就是。”
“这样啊，我知道了。”
老者笑着把委托书交还给乙叶，正当乙叶以为自己又一次被拒绝时，对方走到书桌旁。
“你这个委托书写得太零散了，坐下吧，我们可以先讨论一下这个武器长什么样子。”

……
两个月后的某个傍晚，乙叶郑重地向老者道谢和道别；后者看着她手里那柄长伞，连连叹气。
“明明做了那么漂亮的枪身，竟然用伞面藏起来了。”
乙叶早已摸清了老者脾性，“正是因为它太漂亮了，所以才需要藏起来呀。”
“哎，好话都让你说完了，”老者摆了摆手，“但愿这把武器能助你完成你想做的事。”
“它一定会的，我保证。”

Underground Hollow

On the western edge of the forest outside Flavio City, deep and rhythmic vibrations often rise through the ground at night. Locals say there's a demon down there who loves to strum steel bars, and most people avoid the area.
"Here we are—this is one of my secret hideouts."
"The hollow gathers up my basslines and sends them right back to me. It's a great listener, you know."

地洞

在弗拉维奥城外森林的西侧，一到夜晚，就时常能感受到低沉且有律动的振动透过地面，附近的人都说下面住着一个爱弹钢筋的恶魔，不敢轻易靠近。
“到了，这里就是我的另一处秘密基地啦。”

CharacterArchiveContent.14707.2.en:
Questions for the Divine Messengers

Caramel always carries a few hand-drawn badges in her backpack. They are painted from memory with the resemblance of the Divine Messengers.
During her chance encounter with the two Divine Messengers inside the Monolith—beings said to reflect people's deepest wishes—Caramel, sensed their uniqueness: If the staff of the Monolith represent its will... Then getting close to them might be the key to uncovering Monolith's secrets, right?
Unfortunately, when faced with tough questions like "What does this melody mean?" or "Can you sing?" even the Divine Messengers seem at a loss for words.
CharacterArchiveContent.14707.2.cn:
向神使的提问

焦糖的背包里总是装着几枚画着神使大人的徽章——这是她自己凭着记忆涂的。
自从在星塔里偶遇那两位能映照出人们内心渴望之物的神使大人后，焦糖就意识到了她们的特别——既然星塔的神使代表着星塔的意志……只要和她们搞好关系，岂不是就能从她们嘴里问出更多星塔的秘密？
不过很可惜，面对“这段旋律意味着什么？”“你们会唱歌吗？”这些高难度的提问，即使是神使大人也面露难色。

CharacterArchiveContent.14711.2.en:
"The person I'm most grateful to? That would have to be Miss Caramel."
"Back then, a few of us students started a band on a whim. We knew next to nothing. Almost everything we learned about performing came from Caramel."
"Yeah, Caramel's one of the few...very talkative bassists we've met?"
"Every time she showed up at rehearsal, she'd immediately start sharing her thoughts nonstop, from gear setup to show planning."
"She talked a lot, but everything she said was useful."
"We learned so much from her."
"It was thanks to Caramel that I even realized a bassist could do solos."
"But I heard she rarely shows off those techniques in her performances anymore."
"Kinda miss that, honestly."
"Too bad Caramel always went straight home after shows, and we have no photos with her. Otherwise we could've shown those to you."
"I think it's because she's frugal. After all, living in Flavio is seriously expensive..."
"I heard she even made her own stage outfit."
"Or maybe Caramel-sensei's taste is just...really unique."
"There was this one time we went to visit her, and she happened to be cooking. We thought we could score a free meal, but then we saw her boiling steel wire in a pot..."
"It was horrifying. She was tossing in seasoning while it cooked."
"We figured there was no way we could chew that stuff, so we made an excuse and left."
"Thinking back... it was probably bass strings."
"Aren't strings more expensive than noodles?"
"Oh, I got it then. They weren't for eating. Boiling old strings makes them sound almost like new."
"I see. We thought it was something out of a horror story."
CharacterArchiveContent.14711.2.cn:
“最想感谢的人？那应该是焦糖大人吧。”
“当时我们几个学生一时兴起组乐队，什么都不懂，演出知识可以说全是焦糖教的。”
“确实，焦糖算是我们见过的为数不多的……很健谈的贝斯手？”
“每次一到排练场地就开始发表意见，从设备调试到演出安排这些说个不停。”
“虽然叭叭很多，但是一句废话没有。”
“从她那学到了不少东西。”
“我也是因为焦糖才知道原来贝斯还能独奏。”
“不过听说现在焦糖已经很少在演出时候表演这些技巧了。”
“有点怀念啊。”
“可惜焦糖每次演出结束就回去了，也没有合照什么的，不然还能拿出来给魔女小姐看看。”
“我觉得是她节俭的原因吧，毕竟在弗拉维奥生活的成本真的很高……”
“她那身演出服听说还是自己做的。”
“也可能是焦糖老师的口味太……特别了。”
“就有一次我们去找焦糖，正好赶上她在做饭，本来想顺便蹭饭的，结果看到她在锅里煮铁丝……”
“太可怕了，一边煮还一边往里面放佐料。”
“我们俩感觉应该嚼不动那东西，就找个理由先走了。”
“不过现在回想起来……那东西应该是琴弦。”
“琴弦比面条贵吧？”
“哦你说琴弦我就知道了，是这样，那个不是用来吃的，旧的琴弦煮完以后音色会变好，跟新的差不多。”
“原来如此，还以为是什么恶魔料理。”

CharacterArchiveContent.14712.2.en:
Back when Caramel was a little girl, her father often told her the story of "Midas the Long-Eared."

The tale perhaps had its origin in a former patrician of Flavio—a man who controlled more than half the city's wealth and manpower, and to whom no one dared say "no."
A professional flatterer named Midas spent his days and nights praising the patrician's taste. Naturally, he was handsomely rewarded for it.
When the patrician became interested in music, Midas followed suit, never ceasing his praise. Over time, the patrician came to believe he was the finest musician in all the land.
As the legend has it, one day, while inspecting a new woodland on the outskirts of the city, the patrician heard the voice of a mountain spirit calling to him. The spirit appeared in human form and said: "I've heard you are the most skilled musician. Would you care for a contest?"
Drunk on Midas's flattery, the patrician gladly accepted. He spared no expense and hosted a lavish banquet in the woods, inviting all of the city's elite. Before everyone's eyes, he picked up his best instrument - the flute - and began to play. As the melody echoed in the air, Midas danced beside him with glee, shouting to his loudest: "What magnificent music! What magnificent music! You are the finest musician in the world!"
At that moment, the mountain spirit descended like mist. People say that with a mere gesture, he turned a tree branch into a harp's frame and leaves into strings, then he began to play. The sound was like flowing water, like a bird's song, like a breeze, like the moonlight. All those present were awestruck—even the prideful patrician acknowledge the spirit's supreme skill.
But just as the award ceremony was about to end the competition on a note of harmony and goodwill, Midas's voice cut through and ruined the moment. He shouted: "What's wrong with your ears? What's wrong with your judgement? Are you just scared of the mountain spirit's authority? Was the patrician's music not beautiful?
The mountain spirit was annoyed and gave a cold laugh. "Midas," he said, "do not comment on the things you understand nothing about."
Then he raised his hand and Midas's ears suddenly stretched longer than his two arms!
"Maybe now you'll hear things more clearly," the spirit mocked and vanished like smoke.
Poor Midas was left with ears longer than anyone else's. And indeed, he did hear more clearly. From that day on, he never praised the patrician's playing again. Instead, he often pointed out its flaws—and rather than punishing him, the patrician rewarded him even more handsomely.
"Thank you, Midas," the patrician said. "Thanks to you, I've learned that there's always someone better, always something greater...and that above all, one must speak the truth—especially when it comes to art."

"Is that why our ears are so long, papa?"
"Oh, no, child. But we should learn from Midas the Long-Eared... Especially now, in Flavio, where one's ability to tell the truth matters more than ever."
"But... Aren't they telling the truth now?"
It might be a long time before Caramel can get this question answered.trings in the Pot
CharacterArchiveContent.14712.2.cn:
在焦糖的童年，常听父亲和她说起“长耳朵米达丝”的故事。

故事的原型或许源自弗拉维奥过去的某任城主——那位城主掌控着全城超过半数以上的财富和人力，没人敢在他的面前说“不”字。
一位叫做米达丝的说客就这样日夜吹捧着城主的品味——当然，他也因此获得了丰厚的赏赐。
当城主对乐器燃起兴趣时，他也紧随其后，马屁从未停下……久而久之，城主自然认为，自己就是全天下最厉害的乐手了。
传说某日，城主在城郊视察新开辟的林地时，听到了山神的召唤。山神化作人形，向城主提问说：我听闻，你最擅长奏乐，可否与我比试一二？
早在米达丝的奉承中忘乎所以的城主，欣然答应挑战。他在林地里豪掷千金，大摆宴席，邀请了全城的上流宾客，在众目睽睽之下，他拿起了自己最擅长的笛子，吹奏了起来。笛声在山林之间悠扬环绕，身旁的米达丝高兴的手舞足蹈，他欢呼着：多么伟大的音乐！多么伟大的音乐！您的音乐就是世上最棒的音乐！
山神此时也飘飘然降临，传说他只是一抬手，就将枝条化作琴身，细叶化作琴弦，弹奏起来。琴声如流水，如莺啼，如微风，如月光，令在场众人都不由得拜服——即使是如此骄傲自满的城主，也实在是自愧不如。
没想到，本应握手言和、其乐融融的颁奖，却被米达丝的声音打乱了，他高吼着：“你们的耳朵呢？你们的脑子呢？你们是害怕山神的威风吗？城主的演奏不好听吗？”
山神听完有些愤怒，他冷笑道：米达丝，你不懂的事，不要妄加评论！
说完，他抬手一挥，米达丝的耳朵竟然一下伸得比两手还长！
“这样，你才会听得更清楚一些吧？”山神嘲笑着米达丝，像烟一样消失了。
可怜的米达丝就这样拥有了一对比谁都还长的耳朵——他确实听得更清楚了。自此之后，他再也没有称赞过城主的演奏，反而常常点出了城主演奏中的不足之处——城主非但没有责怪他，反而给了他更多的赏赐，他说：
太感谢了，米达丝，还好有你教会了我，山外有山，人外有人……而且，是你让我明白，任何时候，都得说真话——尤其是对艺术！

“这就是我们的耳朵这么长的原因吗？爸爸”
“噢，不。孩子，不过，我们是该学习一下长耳朵米达丝的教训……尤其是在如今的弗拉维奥，能说真话，非常重要。”
“不过，现在真是这样吗……？”
焦糖的疑问，或许还需要很多时间才能得到回答。

CharacterArchiveContent.14713.2.en:
Flavio wasn't always the city it is today. It was once a place famous for its craftsmanship and spice.
After a new spice source was discovered in the northern forests, the city-state lord hired many workers to help with spice harvesting and transportation. Caramel's parents were among those who joined the rush. As Flufla, they had sharp senses of smell and hearing.
More and more people gathered in Flavio, but each's share of the profit pie kept shrinking. Caramel's parents soon turned their eyes to the Monolith—the rapid growth of the city-state, the booming spice trade, and the rise of Scarlet Sights Media presented a prime opportunity for commerce and entertainment to flourish, and the subsequent demand for Artifacts meant that a wave of "Trekker fever" would follow.
After becoming Trekkers, Caramel's parents were able to build a stable home life. Then, on Flavio Day of Nebula Month, Caramel was born. She grew up alongside Flavio's expansion, shaped by the influence of her Trekker parents.
When Caramel secretly followed her parents into the Monolith for the first time, she was instantly drawn in by the Monolith's strange, dreamlike sounds. Drumbeats and deep, piercing rhythms flowed into her keen ears from the empty air overhead, the ground beneath her, and every corner around her.
One day, after stumbling across a Stella Drama inside the Monolith, Caramel recognized it at last: the deep, entrancing sound that had fascinated her was coming from the instrument held by the person on the screen—an instrument with four thick strings.
Even so, at the time, she still didn't know what the instrument was called—it looked a little like a guitar, but the sound was far deeper.
Years later, standing as an established Trekker before the Wishing Box, she could only dig through her hazy memories of those sounds and images, then putting the wish finally into words:
"I want to play the sound of the Monolith."
When she left the Monolith that day, Caramel was cradling her beloved instrument in her arms. Looking down at it, she remembered a story her father had told her not long ago. She decided she would become a musician who always "tell the truth."
"I'll call you Midas."
CharacterArchiveContent.14713.2.cn:
弗拉维奥在以前，并非是现在的模样，而是一个靠手工和香料制作闻名的城市。
自从在北部森林里发现了新的香料来源，城邦主就雇佣了许多人来帮助开采和运输。焦糖的双亲就是在这一时期，加入到采伐赚钱的浪潮，他们作为绒绒族，有着聪敏的嗅觉和听觉。
聚集在弗拉维奥的人越来越多，每个人到手的朵拉却越来越少。焦糖的双亲转而把目光投向了星塔——城邦的壮大、香料业的发达、以及绯瞳传讯的发展，让商业和娱乐业在此地野蛮生长，由此带来的神器缺口，必然会掀起一阵“旅人热”。
焦糖的双亲作为旅人活跃之后，他们的生活也逐渐安定下来，焦糖就在这之后的一个雾月、弗拉维奥日出生了——伴随着弗拉维奥的成长，焦糖也在这旅人家庭的影响下成长着。
在焦糖第一次偷偷跟着父母进入星塔“冒险”的时候，她就被星塔里那些奇妙又充满想象力的声音吸引了。那些鼓点，以及低沉却极具穿透力的律动，从空荡荡的头顶、脚底、四周，不断的传进她灵敏的耳朵。
在一次偶然观看到星塔里放映的影戏后，焦糖确认了，那让她着迷的低沉的声响，是画面里那人手中有四根粗弦的乐器发出的。
尽管如此，焦糖那时还并不知道那个乐器该如何称呼——它似乎和吉他长得有些像，但声音却过于的低沉了。
多年以后，当她作为一个成熟的旅人站在许愿箱前时，只能试图尽可能地在模糊的回忆里寻找那些听到过的声响、画面，并口述她藏在心中多年的愿望：
“我想要，演奏星塔的声音。”
从星塔出来的时候，焦糖怀里已经抱着她心爱的乐器了——焦糖看着它，想起了不久前父亲给自己讲过的故事，她决定要成为一个“说真话”的乐手。
“就叫你，‘米达丝’吧。”

CharacterArchiveContent.14911.2.en:
The children clambered over the fence and rushed toward the playground.
The boys were always the most excited, scrambling to claim their favorite rides, while the girls held hands with each other and ran to the quieter corners.
A frail girl straggled behind them. She ran slower than everyone else. After only a few steps, tiny beads of sweat rolled down her thin cheeks.
"Sorry, we ran too fast. Want me to pull you along?"
"It's fine... I-I just need a moment to catch my breath..."

The others came back for her, reaching out their hands. She did her best to grip theirs in return.
She often remembered how, on that summer day, what she saw above wasn't the silver-colored playground equipment but drifting clouds under a boundless blue sky.

"This is boring. Let's build sandcastles today."
"Did you bring water? You can't build them without water."
"Ah! I—I left in a rush and forgot..."
"It's... It's okay. Maybe we can build the sand castles without water..."

She crouched down and carefully scooped a handful of sand into her palms. But it sifted through her fingers, carried off by the wind only to fall back into the pit.
Frustrated, she tried again, but the same thing happened.

"See? It won't work without water! Let's go fetch some!"
"Wait, don't go..."
"Leave it to us. You stay here. No point for you to follow us."
"No... Don't leave me alone..."

She watched as they left, and a tangled emotion welled up inside her.
It was disgust at her own body, but also jealousy at seeing others walking closely.
It wasn't the first time she'd been treated differently, and she knew it wouldn't be the last.
She had lost count of how many times she'd had this thought. And when that unease pressed too hard against her heart, something long-repressed finally began to break loose.
She felt the restlessness take form, swelling, spreading outward from within her until everything around her fell silent.

The change struck her in a flash...
By the time she came to, the world before her was no longer familiar.
The trees that once shaded her were laying toppled across the streets,
the playground equipment was bent and twisted, jammed into buildings,
Screams replaced the birds and cicadas, and her friends were nowhere to be found.
She lifted her gaze skyward: it was neither blue nor white, but a hue of red that looked almost black.
No laughter echoed in the playground anymore, only an incomprehensible noise of chaos.
The summer heat grew unbearable, as if it meant to burn everything to ash...

At last, she began to understand what was happening. She tried to stand, to run, but her body would not move.
Looking down, she saw the sandy pit had become a scatter of broken stained glass,
reflecting a twisted world—and her own face, blurred beyond recognition.
CharacterArchiveContent.14911.2.cn:
孩子们跨过围栏，奔向公园的游乐场，
男孩们总是很兴奋，他们争先抢占喜欢的设施，女孩们则手牵着手，小跑来到几处安静的角落。
人群后有一个瘦小的身影，她比其他孩子跑得都要慢，没几步，豆粒大的汗珠就顺着她瘦削的脸颊滑落。
“抱歉，我们跑太快了，要我拉你吗？”
“没事的……我，我喘一会……”

同伴们折回来，向她伸出手，而她同样尽全力回握对方。
她时常记起，与大家共同度过的那个夏日里，抬头看见的不是银白的设施，而是无垠蓝天下的朵朵流云。

“其他几个都玩腻了，今天我们来堆沙堡吧。”
“那你带了水吗？没水可堆不起沙堡啊。”
“呜呀！我，我出门急，忘了……”
“没，没事……没水，说不定也能玩……”

她蹲下，小心翼翼地将一团沙土捧在手心，流沙却顺着她指尖飘落，被风吹散又落回沙坑中，
她有些懊恼，再次尝试，还是同样的结果。

“看吧，没水根本玩不了，我们得去打水啦！”
“等一下，别走……”
“交给我们吧，你就在这等着，不用跟过来。”
“不要，留下我一个人……”

望着同伴们离开的背影，她的内心涌现出一股复杂的情绪。
无论是对自己身体的厌恶，还是见到其他人牵手时的嫉妒。
她知道自己不是第一次被“特殊对待”，自然也不会是最后一次。
已经不记得是第几次产生这样的想法， 当这份不安催动内心，一直被压抑的某种东西终于开始了暴走。
她感到那份躁动凝聚成型，膨胀，由身体里向外扩散，直到周围的一切都安静下来。

变故发生的时候，一切都来得太过突然……
当她回过神来，她眼前的世界早已不再是熟悉的模样。
平日里庇荫的大树吹倒在人们行走的街道上，
公园内玩耍的设施正以扭曲的姿态镶在楼房，
人们的尖叫替代了鸟声与蝉鸣，昔日的伙伴也早就不见了踪影。
她抬头看向天空，既不是蓝，也不是白，而是偏黑的红。
公园里不再回荡欢声笑语，只有无法理解的混乱杂音。
夏天变得异常燥热，似要将周围的一切烧尽……

终于，她开始理解眼前的事物，想要站起身逃跑，却发现自己再也无法动弹，
她看向自己的脚下，原本是一片沙土的小坑，却变成了一片片碎裂的彩窗，
倒映着歪曲的世界，和她那分不清模样的脸。

CharacterArchiveContent.14912.2.en:
Gerie opened her eyes, but everything was still pitch-black. She could hear the hum of several Artifacts running at once,
then a streak of white light split through the darkness. Grabbing hold of its edge, Gerie used every ounce of strength to pull herself free.
At last, she crawled down the altar.

Her bare feet touched the cold floor. The chill she got was enough to make her happy, because it was proof that the excess magic had been purged. The results would only last a week, but for a few days she could feel what it was like to live as an ordinary person.
Without even changing into her novice habit, Gerie sprinted toward the Grand Sanctum in her ritual whites. The choir faltered at her sudden intrusion, but Gerie filled her lungs with all the air she could and shouted in her loudest voice—"Don't mind me! Please continue!"
Then she gasped for breath until she nearly passed out.
She savored this sensation. After she was taken in by Grace Imperium, she learned her fate and the price she had to pay—a sliver of her freedom, traded for treatment that would keep her alive. Ever since then, she had but a single thought.
"As long as I get to live, this isn't so bad."
She no longer cursed fate, and she gave up trying to trace its causes. She only wanted to experience, as much as possible, what being alive felt like.

"How many times have I told you? Don't run around in that outfit!"
An elderly woman hauled her up. She wore a nun's robe, but her authority was no less than a bishop's.
"S-sorry... Mother, I was just released today..."
The old nun looked over her frail body and sighed.
"Never mind. After you eat, remember to come back and clean the chapel. No freeloading allowed if you want to stay here."
"Mother, what are we eating today?"
"I made you extra-spicy porridge. You can't taste much else, right?"
"No, please... Last time you cut peppers, you were coughing for so long..."
"You've always been a bother, and now you worry about me? Just eat it."
Stubborn as ever, Gerie would not just sit and eat the food quietly. She tried to help fetch the knives, only to cut her hand by accident.
The old nun stayed calm. She pulled out alcohol and cloth from her pocket to treat the wound, as though she had done so countless times before.
"You heal fast and say you don't feel the pain. So you think you're made of iron?"
Gerie stayed silent. She didn't want to argue. She only watched the old nun's calloused hands carefully cleaning her wound.
Only in moments like this could she feel a proper child.

"You need to learn some life skills. You can't rely on me forever."
"But you wouldn't let me handle the knives just now... Ah!"
"That's different. The higher-ups only see you as a tool, but someone has to teach you how to live... Let's start with shelling beans."
"And after the beans? Washing vegetables, baking bread, and, and..."
"One thing at a time. You'll learn everything I teach you, and then you won't need to depend on me anymore."
CharacterArchiveContent.14912.2.cn:
格芮睁开眼，面前却仍是一片漆黑，她能听见数个神器同时运作的声音，
随着一道白光划破黑暗，格芮攀住光的边缘，用尽全身力气将身体探出黑暗。
终于，她从祭坛上爬了出来。

格芮光着脚踩在地板上，她能感觉到有些冰凉，光是这点便足以让她感到开心，因为这代表多余的魔力已经清除，虽然治疗效果仅能持续一周，但她能在这几天里体验正常人拥有的感觉。
还来不及换上见习修者的制服，格芮便穿着举行仪式时的白衣跑去了大圣所，唱诗班被她的突然闯入打乱了节奏，格芮却几乎是将能吸入的空气都纳入肺部，尽最高的嗓音喊道——“不用在意我！请继续！”
然后大口喘着粗气，喘到就快要晕厥过去。
她很享受这样的感觉：自从被收容，得知了自己的命运，以及只需要牺牲小小自由的代价，又能得到周期性的治疗后，格芮的心中便只有一个念头。
“只要活下去就好了，其实这样也不算坏。”
不再憎恶命运，不去揣测因果，她只是想要尽可能体验活着的实感。

“跟你说了多少遍了，不要穿着这件衣服到处乱跑！”
一位年迈的老者将她提了起来，她穿着修者的衣服，但从威严上却与主教无异。
“对，对不起……嬷嬷，我今天才刚被放出来……”
老修者看着她瘦弱的身体，又叹了口气。
“算了，等会吃完东西记得来打扫圣所。想在这里生活，可不能光吃白饭。”
“嬷嬷，今天我们吃什么？”
“给你准备了特辣的汤粥，你不是尝不出其他味道吗？”
“不要……嬷嬷上次切辣椒咳了好一阵子。”
“你尽给别人添乱，还担心起我了？老老实实吃就行了。”
倔强的她不甘在一旁看着，想要帮忙取刀具时，却不小心划伤了手。
老修者不慌不忙，从口袋里拿出酒精和棉布为她处理伤口，好像这样的事情已经重复多次。
“伤口好得快，不怕疼，就真把自己当铁皮疙瘩了？”
格芮不再说话了，她也不想狡辩，只是看着老修者用满是老茧的手擦拭自己的伤。
只有在这种时候，她才能体验到本属于这个年纪的任性。

“你得学点生活的本领了，不能什么事都得靠我。我养不了你一辈子。”
“那您刚才还不让我用刀……呀！”
“这是两码事。上边的人只把你当耗材可不行，总得有人教你什么是生活……先从剥豆子开始吧。”
“剥完豆子之后呢？洗菜，烤面包，还有，还有……”
“慢慢来，我教的你都能学会，到时候就不用再依赖我咯。”

CharacterArchiveContent.14913.2.en:
"This is what you came up with? Are you mocking me!?"
In one of the Dusk Arbiters' chambers, the blacksmith tore Gerie's submitted weapon design into shreds.
Unbothered, Gerie calmly pulled out another identical set of blueprints from within her novice habit—
It was a weapon that could change its form: Able to pass as an iron shovel, yet with a mechanism that split its hollow interior to transform into a retractable chain blade.
"You're so heartless. I spent all night on that~"
"Sigh~ Could it be that you actually enjoy breaking what others treasure?"

Hidden blades, poison daggers, throwing knives... The man had overseen the development of countless weapons, and he knew immediately what he was looking at.
The weapon Gerie designed had but one purpose—to wound without killing outright.
"The Arbiters require missions carried out with efficiency, not someone like you treating battle as entertainment!"
"But I'm like this. And you know that not only do I always finish my missions, I can also extract valuable intel without executing the enemy."
Gerie smiled at him with unabashed confidence as she played with her hair.
"I'll admit your methods work sometimes. But most of the time, even with targets who didn't matter, you did not strike them down. Which makes all this just excuses for your twisted tastes!"
"Look at this design. Instead of reinforcing it for lethal efficiency, why waste effort on making it transform?"
"Hehe~ But if the fight ends in one stroke, isn't that boring?"

The man could hardly believe that someone with a mind as unsound as hers had risen to the position of Chief Arbiter.
Worse still, he could imagine what damage it would do to his belief if such a frivolous weapon were actually approved.
"Enough! The fact that the Chief Justice favors you doesn't mean you can break all the rules. If not for your last assigned weapon being ruined in the endurance test—"
"... Wait, that rampage wasn't an accident? You did it on purpose, just to get the excuse to design something new..."
"There are some things you really shouldn't dig into~ Who knows? If another 'incident' were to happen here, people might just call it one of my little fits~"
"As the most outstanding and authoritative blacksmith here, is getting a nice toy for an Arbiter really too much to ask of you?"

Gerie pushed the door open and stepped out, her face split with a grin she couldn't hide. The novice nun, who had been waiting outside for some time, hurried over and took the design plans from Gerie's hand.
"How did it go? Did they approve it?"
"Of course~ Thanks to you helping me design it, all credit to you, little Tessa."
"No, no! Being able to assist you is already a great honor!"
"It's just... there's one thing I don't understand. Why go through all this trouble? Is it really just so you could 'enjoy' fighting?"
"... Life is too short. The words we want to say, the things we want to do... Most of the time, we never get the chance."
"One's will to live is the fiercest when death is staring them in the face. That's why I show my enemies mercy, so they can fight for another breath."
"I... I don't understand..."
"And besides, watching people claw and struggle to live... It makes me so very happy. Fufu~~ Hahaha~~~"
Light on her feet, Gerie skipped down the sunset-lit corridor, not caring at all about the stares around her.
As Tessa watched her go, she couldn't help but wonder—was Gerie well and truly delirious, as the rumors claimed?
CharacterArchiveContent.14913.2.cn:
“把这样的东西给我，你是在戏弄我吗！？”
黄昏裁判的某个房间内，铁匠将格芮递来的武器需求设计图撕了个粉碎。
格芮不慌不忙，又从修者服内掏出另一本同样的设计图——
那是一把可变形的武器，既能伪装成铁铲，也能通过机关分割中空的内部，变为一把伸缩自如的链刃。
“您可真是无情，把人家辛苦通宵做好的东西就这么轻易毁掉了~”
“唉~难道您有特殊的癖好，喜欢把别人珍视的东西轻易破坏吗？”

袖剑，毒匕，飞刀……参与过无数武器的研发，看着眼前的设计图纸，男人自是理解：
格芮的这把武器，设计目的只有一个——“有杀伤力却可以不致命”。
“审判官需要高效率地解决目标，而不是像你这样，把战斗当作乐趣！”
“但就是我这样的人，不仅每次都能完成组织的任务，还能在不处刑敌人的情况下套出重要的情报。”
格芮满不在意，玩弄着头发，朝对方露出自信的笑容。
“我承认有几次采用这样的方式是不错，但大多数无关紧要的人，你都没能下狠手，这是你为自己恶趣味开脱的诡辩！”
“看看你提出的设计，明明可以往一击毙命的方向强化，为什么要多余添加可变形的功能。”
“呼呼~战斗要是一下子就结束不就没有意思了嘛~”

男人无法想象，这样一个精神都谈不上正常的人是如何爬到首席审判官的位置，
更无法想象，若是应了她的愿，造出这样一件玩闹性质的武器，将会对他的理念造成怎样的冲击。
“够了！不要以为裁判长青睐你，就可以无法无天了。要不是之前预定给你的武器在测试里被弄坏——”
“……所以那次暴走不是意外？你在装疯卖傻，只是为了重新研制新的武器……”
“有些事情不要过问太多~保不准，这里接下来要发生的命案，也会被理解成是我的暴走导致的~”
“作为黄昏裁判里最杰出、最权威的铁匠，为审判官添置一件趁手的玩具应该不是什么难事吧。”

格芮推门而出，脸上已是挂着难掩的笑意，在门外等候多时的见习修者凑了上来，接下格芮递过的设计图。
“前，前辈！怎么样了，申请书通过了吗！？”
“当然~多亏了你陪我一起设计这个武器，谢啦~小泰莎。”
“没有没有！能帮上格芮前辈的忙，是我的荣幸！”
“只是……有一点我不明白。您饶了这么大的弯子，真的只是为了去享受战斗吗？”
“……生命太短暂了，想说的话，想做的事，多数时候都来不及。”
“人只有在感到性命受到威胁的时候，才会爆发出强烈的求生欲，所以我愿意宽恕敌人，给他们喘息的机会。”
“格芮前辈……？”
“不过，看着为活命而挣扎的人，也是一件很幸福的事。呼呼~~呵呵呵~~~”
格芮在夕阳的楼道中轻快跳着，丝毫不在意周围人投来的异样目光。
望着她的背影，泰莎不由得心想——这个人，真的如传闻一样疯了吗？

CharacterArchiveContent.15011.2.en:
Laru is always going on about her so-called "All-Fish Feast" when she's out fishing.

"Just wait, tonight's dinner is gonna be an all-fish feast~"
"I could feel it when I cast the line—today's definitely an all-fish feast day."
"You have no idea. I've been so lucky lately, I'm almost sick of all-fish feasts."

So, what exactly is in an all-fish feast? Sashimi? Steamed, braised, sweet-and-sour fish fillets? Fish balls? Fish head tofu soup?
Laru just grins at the guesses and says nothing.

Today's another big haul. She struts down the street with an eight-pound fish, bragging to anyone who'll listen, including the horse standing by the road and the dog dozing at the shop door.
She hums all the way home. "Another all-fish feast coming right up."
When she gets home, she builds a fire in her backyard with practiced ease. The knife dances in her hands—guts out, scales off, the fish split open and set on a rack like a flying carpet spread wide above the flames.
She sprinkles sea salt over the sizzling, golden skin.

But tonight, no one's around to share the haul. The smell of grilled fish drifts into the night air, luring a stray cat to perch on the wall, drooling.
Laru generously tears off a chunk of tail and offers it to the kitten.
"An all-fish feast just means a feast made entirely of fish, isn't it?"

She sits down to enjoy her hard-earned dinner, only to see the cat sniff the fish, paw at it twice, and then walk away.
"Huh?! What's gotten into you, you little furball?! Wasting food is a crime!"
But the cat doesn't look back. Clearly, it's decided there's nothing edible here.
"Rude... You don't know good food when it's shoved right in front of you. This is Laru's personally caught, personally cooked grilled fish! Fine, more for me... mm—mmph?! Ptui!"

Laru spits it out, her eyes suddenly widening. She grabs her chopsticks and pokes at the fish's head.
"I can't believe I forgot to check... This is a Stinkyfish? You can't eat this!"
CharacterArchiveContent.15011.2.cn:
菈露钓鱼的时候总把“全鱼宴”挂在嘴边。

“等着啊，今天钓到的鱼晚上给大伙做全鱼宴~”
“我今天甩竿的时候就觉得，今天必将能有一顿全鱼宴。”
“你都不知道，我最近太走运了，全鱼宴吃得有点腻了。”

全鱼宴都有什么？
刺生凉拌？清蒸红烧糖醋？鱼丸鱼头豆腐汤？
菈露对这些揣测都笑而不语。

今天也是大丰收的一天。
菈露举着她那条足足八斤大鱼，和路过的每一个人炫耀，连路边站着的马和店门口趴着的狗都没放过。
她一路哼着歌，念叨着今晚又是全鱼宴的一天。
等她回到自己的住所，熟练地在自己家后院堆起篝火。小刀在她手中飞舞，剔去内脏，刮掉鱼鳞，剖开的大鱼穿上支架，像一张张开的飞毯，悬停在篝火之上。
她给烤得冒油的鱼撒上海盐。

但今天没有人跟她一起分享收获的喜悦，只有烤鱼的香气随着袅袅炊烟飘散，馋得流浪的小猫趴院墙上流着口水。
菈露大方地把一大块鱼尾送给它。
“只有鱼的晚宴，就是全鱼宴，难道不是吗？”
她坐下准备享用今天的劳动成果，却发现流浪猫闻了闻她给的鱼，最后扒拉了两下，转头离开了。
“嗯？？？你这小猫怎么回事？！浪费食物是可耻！”
但流浪猫离开得毫不留恋，似乎已经断定这里没有食物。
“真是的……没有品味的小猫，这可是菈露大人亲自钓起来亲自料理的烤鱼！你不吃我自己吃……唔……唔唔？呸、呸呸……这什么怪味？？”
菈露把刚吃进口的烤鱼吐出来，突然像是意识到什么，用筷子翻看了一下条大鱼的鱼头。
“……大意了，怎么是不能吃的臭臭鱼啊！！”

CharacterArchiveContent.15012.2.en:
"If you can already score a 90, why not push a little harder and aim for a perfect score next time?"
Young Laru looked up at her parents' expectant eyes and, for the first time, began to doubt her own excellence.
She had the highest score in the entire class. She beat everyone. Her teachers praised her, her parents were proud of her, and everyone around her said she was amazing.
But before she even had a chance to feel proud, everyone said the same thing.
—You'll definitely do even better next time, right?
—You're so smart, you'll grow up to be someone really impressive, right?
—These mistakes were just from carelessness. If you focus a bit more, a perfect score is totally within reach, right?
...
...

But I already got first place! Shouldn't you be proud of me?
She envied the neighbor girl, who barely scraped by with passing grades but whose parents praised her without hesitation, as if just passing was already something to celebrate.
Why?
Little Laru didn't understand. She just felt wronged.

Later, as she got older, Laru began to understand.
She was too good.
Her achievements weren't just her own. Her parents, her teachers, everyone around her—they all had a stake in them.
And so, every "next time" came with expectation—an endless string of "next times" to keep the spotlight burning.
But that was exhausting, wasn't it?
Twelve-year-old Laru leaned against the windowsill. She watched the neighbor girl—her same age—skip out the door, clearly headed off for a picnic with friends.
"Must be nice. Just barely pass and never have to deal with anyone's expectations..."
Then it hit her. Laru found the perfect solution.
What if she always just barely passed...?
If she stayed average, kept her head down, wasn't too good—maybe she could be carefree like that girl too.
And so, at age twelve, Laru discovered her life philosophy.

"Hello—Ma'am, yes, it's me, Laru. Oh, you said I left early? Actually...I had to meet with a very important client tonight.
"Yes, a very important one. They insisted, so I had no choice but to attend... Y-yes, it's all wrapped up now, I'm heading back to the office."
Laru hangs up. The angler next to her shakes their head.
"Looks like your slacking time's up."
"Well, I caught plenty today. Here, take the bucket~"
Laru stretches and cheerfully hands over all the fish she caught, then begins packing up.
The evening breeze is crisp. She does the math in her head as she walks back.
An hour and a half left till the end of the workday. The trip back takes twenty minutes. Today's tasks will take about forty. That still leaves a good thirty minutes to slack off.
"Another day, perfectly optimized for slacking~♪"
CharacterArchiveContent.15012.2.cn:
“既然都能考九十分了，努力一下，下次争取到满分吧？”
年幼的菈露迎着父母期待的目光，第一次对自己的优秀产生了怀疑。
她的成绩是这次考核中最优秀的，她赢过了所有人，老师称赞她，父母夸奖她，远亲近友都在说她厉害。
但还没等她开始骄傲得意，所有人都说了同一件事。
——下次一定可以拿到更好的成绩吧？
——你这么优秀，将来长大一定很了不起吧？
——这些错误都是因为你粗心大意，如果能再细心一点，完全是有可能满分的吧？
……
……

但我已经是第一了啊！不应该为我骄傲吗？
她羡慕邻居家的小孩，虽然成绩只是堪堪及格，但她的父母每次都会毫不吝啬地夸她，好像只要刚好六十分就已经很厉害了。
为什么呢？
年幼的菈露只觉得委屈。

后来，随着年龄增长，菈露慢慢理解了。
她太优秀了。
她的出色已经不仅是自己的荣誉，也是旁人的骄傲，是父母的脸面，是师长的自豪。
所以有无数的名为“下一次”的期待落在她身上，只有无数的“下一次”才能带来永不落幕的荣光。
但那也太累了吧？
十二岁的菈露趴在窗台前，看着邻居那个和她同龄的女孩兴高采烈地跑出家门，听上去她今天要和朋友出去野餐。
“真好啊，只要一直考个及格分，就不会背负他人的期待……”
菈露灵光一闪，忽然发现自己找到了最优解。
只要一直是及格分就好了……？
只要她只是刚好及格，无功无过，没有那么优秀，那她就可以和那个女孩一样无忧无虑地出去玩耍。
十二岁的菈露在这一天找到了自己的人生哲学。

“喂——领导，是、我是菈露。呃，您说早退是吗？其实是……因为今晚有个重要的客户需要接待。
“对，很重要的客户，对方盛情邀请，我只好去应酬一下……是、是，现在已经结束了，我正打算回公司呢。”
菈露挂了通讯，身边的钓友摇着头看她。
“看来你的摸鱼时间结束了。”
“反正今天的鱼也钓够了，这桶送给你了~”
菈露伸了个懒腰，大方地把今天钓到的鱼都分给了其他人，然后收拾东西开始往回走。
傍晚的微风带着凉意，菈露盘算着时间。
现在距离下班时间还有一个半小时，从这里回到办公室还要二十分钟，今天的工作大概只需要四十分钟就能处理完，还能再摸三十分钟。
“今天也是充分利用时间摸鱼的一天~ ♪”

CharacterArchiveContent.15013.2.en:
Grace Imperium is giving all official personnel a full round of weapon maintenance, using better materials and more advanced techniques to significantly boost both performance and lethality.
"I bet some bored idiot sweet-talked the Senate into approving the budget, then quietly skimmed a little off the top."
Laru sits on Willow's desk, mechanically munching on fries while glumly staring at her weapon—a lance that used to feel just right in her hands. After this so-called "maintenance," sure, the power's gone up, but thanks to whatever mystery material they forged in, the whole thing is now ridiculously heavy.
"There's no way I can use this to fish anymore!!"
"Was the lance ever supposed to be used for fishing in the first place?"
Willow doesn't even look up from her paperwork. Laru is a friend who keeps turning up in her office to slack off.
"You don't get it..."
Laru lets out another sigh.
As in every corporation, Grace Imperium has countless pointless rules—one of them being that assigned weapons are considered part of a person's identity. Even if you hate yours, you still have to carry it around.
When Laru first joined Grace Imperium, she immediately picked this lance from the limited options available. It was the perfect size, weight and balance—easy to carry, and if you just tied on some fishing line and a hook, bam: instant fishing rod.
It was practically made for her.
But now, the lance is way too heavy for fishing. And with how long it is, even carrying it feels like a chore.
After Laru's third dramatic sigh, Willow finally glances up from her work.
"Grace Imperium doesn't forbid personal weapon modifications, does it?"
That snaps Laru out of her funk.
"You mean..."
Willow pulls a blank sheet of paper from her desk, scribbles down a name, and hands it over.
"The Trekker Association recently pulled some really strong, lightweight materials from the Monolith. Go ask Horizon if there's any left. If there is, take it to this person at the Starlight Research Institute. She can help you mod it—though you'll have to pay for it yourself."
"Oooh! You're still the queen of contacts and inside info! I'll bring you fries next time~"
Laru takes the note, thanks Willow, and leaves the same way she came—vaulting through the window in a blaze of energy.

Half a month later, Laru sends someone to deliver Willow a grilled fish and three bags of fries, along with a thank-you note:
"My very first catch since I got Silver Gull re-modded~ Enjoy~"
CharacterArchiveContent.15013.2.cn:
恩赐意志给所有在编人员都进行了一次武器保养，用了更好的材料和更先进的技术，确保武器的性能和杀伤力都有了质的提升。
“感觉完全就是哪个吃饱了没事干的家伙，哄着元老院批了预算，再偷偷从中获利。”
菈露坐在薇洛的办公桌上，一边机械地吃着薯条，一边满脸愁容地看着她的武器——那柄原本非常趁手的武器，经过一番“保养”，威力是有了，但不知道被替换了什么新材料，整个长枪变得笨重无比。
“现在这个样子，根本没办法拿来钓鱼啊！！”
“那本来也不是应该拿来钓鱼的吧？”
薇洛低头工作，随口应和着这位时不时就会跑来她办公室里偷懒的友人。
“唉，你不懂……”
菈露叹了口气。
恩赐意志总有一些多余又无聊的规则，比如人员配备的武器是统一分配的，那是身份象征的一部分，即便你再不喜欢，也得随身携带。
菈露当年入职恩赐意志时，在仅有的可选武器类型中，一眼就看中了这柄长枪，不轻不重，长度刚好，非常适合随身携带，只要系上鱼线鱼钩，就可以直接拿来当钓竿用。
简直是为她量身定制的武器。
但如今，这柄长枪的重量已经完全不适合拿来钓鱼，甚至碍于它的长度，随身携带都显得碍事。
薇洛在她第三次重重叹气的时候，终于从工作中抬头看了她一眼。
“你们恩赐意志并没有规定，不能私改武器吧？”
她的话音刚落，菈露突然来了精神。
“你的意思是……”
薇洛从办公桌上抽出一张白纸，快速地在上面写下一个名字，然后递给了菈露。
“地理协会前不久从星塔里找到了一些硬度不错，但重量很轻的材料，你去找彼岸问问，如果还有，你可以拿着那些材料，去星辉学馆找这个人，她会帮你改——当然，这其中的费用你要自己解决。”
“哦哦！你的人脉和消息还是这么厉害！下次给你带包薯条~”
菈露接过纸条，行动派的她向薇洛道了谢，像她来时那样，风风火火地翻窗户离开了。

半个月后，菈露托人给薇洛送来了一条烤鱼和三包薯条，并附上了感谢信：
“这可是用改装过的长枪钓起来的第一条鱼~要吃哦~”
